emitters.name: 519A
emitters.notes_html: The all-round gold standard. Wide range of CCTs (roughly 2700K–5700K), neutral to rosy tint. Floody with the dome on. Easily dedomed for more throw, a lower CCT and a rosier tint. "V1" is the newer, preferred revision (BLF Guide, Emisar).

best_for.also_html: Luminus SST-20 (4000K 95 CRI), Samsung LH351D, Cree XP-L HI, Lumileds HL2X, LatticePower TN3535 (budget)
best_for.why_html: High CRI, easy to drive and a great tint, with enough throw for everyday use. The alternatives trade some colour quality or tint consistency for price
Small cells supply little current, so colour and efficiency at low drive matter more than maximum output. The 219B/219F dislike high current, which is fine here

best_for.hint: D4-, KR4-, FW3- and TS10-style lights
best_for.why_html: Several small high-CRI dies behind a multi-TIR give a smooth, floody beam; tiny dies (E21A, CSP2323, XP-G2) suit micro triples

best_for.also_html: NTG35, Nichia B35AM, Nichia E21A, Nichia 144A, FFL5009D, LatticePower TN3535 (90 CRI), Lumileds HL2X
best_for.why_html: Wide, even beam with good colour at modest output. Domed parts behind a TIR or mule give the smoothest flood
R9080-class colour (Ra 95+, high R9) renders reds, skin and wood correctly. Check Duv too: very rosy parts tint everything pink

emitters.name: 219B
emitters.notes_html: Legendary rosy tint (especially the sw45k 4500K bin). Low output and dislikes high current; largely replaced by 519A / NTG35 (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: 219C
emitters.notes_html: Sold in 3000K, 3500K, 4000K, 5000K and 5700K (Ledrise). The brighter but less-talented successor to the 219B; itself largely superseded by the SST-20 and LH351D (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: 219F
emitters.notes_html: Successor to the 219C; best known for an 1800K sodium-lamp-like version. Doesn't like being overdriven (BLF Guide).

best_for.why_html: Small cells supply little current, so colour and efficiency at low drive matter more than maximum output. The 219B/219F dislike high current, which is fine here

emitters.name: B35AM
emitters.notes_html: Four tiny dies with a natural, sunlight-like tint. R9080 bins span 2700K–6500K (BLF test). Its odd footprint needs a dedicated MCPCB, which limits overdrive (BLF Guide).

best_for.why_html: R9080-class colour (Ra 95+, high R9) renders reds, skin and wood correctly. Check Duv too: very rosy parts tint everything pink

best_for.also_html: NTG35, Nichia B35AM, Nichia E21A, Nichia 144A, FFL5009D, LatticePower TN3535 (90 CRI), Lumileds HL2X

emitters.name: 719A
emitters.notes_html: Flat (domeless) emitter with two stacked dies, usually sold in 4000K or 5000K (BLF 4000K test, BLF 5000K test). Colour like a dedomed 519A with more output but a floodier beam; generally considered underwhelming (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: 144A
emitters.notes_html: Nichia's answer to the XHP50 (different footprint, no thermal pad). High CRI but strong tint shift without diffusion; used in the Armytek Wizard C2 Pro Nichia, which is 4500K (Armytek, BLF Guide).

emitters.name: SFT-25R
emitters.notes_html: 5000K, 5700K or 6500K (samples run cooler than nominal), plus a 5700K 90 CRI WG version (Luminus datasheet, BLF WG test). Small round die (about half the SFT-40's area) = extreme throw; out-throws the SFT-40 in the same host. Standard 3535 footprint fits most EDC/thrower boards (BLF test, Convoy).

best_for.also_html: Luminus SFT-40, Osram W2, Cree XP-L HI, Cree XP-LR, LMP W5050SQ5, YinDing 5050 Glass, Luminus SFT-12

best_for.also_html: Osram W1, Luminus SFT-40, Luminus SFT-42R, Cree XM-MR, Convoy F45R, Luminus SFT-60
best_for.why_html: A big reflector multiplies luminance, so high-luminance dies that take more current win. The SFT-42R only comes into its own in large heads

emitters.name: SFT-40
emitters.notes_html: Domeless all-round thrower king: punchy hotspot with usable spill. 6500K leans green, 5000K is decent, and 3000K is the high-CRI version (BLF Guide, Convoy).

candela.beam_html: Best all-round thrower hotspot (more usable spill than SFT-25R)

best_for.why_html: Best hotspot-to-spill balance; the multi-die alternatives give a wider spot and more lumens for less throw
Rosy (FFL) or warm 95 CRI (SFT-40/70) alternatives to cool-white throwers; the YinDing is the rare cool-white high-CRI round die

emitters.name: SFT-60
emitters.notes_html: 5000K/5700K/6500K, 6.0 mm² die, 15 A max. High Vf (~3.3 V @ 10 A, ~3.5 V @ 15 A per one user), so a single-cell buck driver may not reach full current. Sits between SFT-40 and SFT-90 (Convoy).

emitters.name: SFT-42R
emitters.notes_html: 5000–6500K (Luminus). Round-die thrower with a bigger hotspot than SFT-40 and ~2 A more draw. Best in large reflectors (Convoy L21B); in TIR or small hosts it throws less than the SFT-40. Phosphor is more brittle than other SFT parts, so don't let a TIR press on it (Convoy).

emitters.notes_html: 6500K only; a pre-production sample measured green (Duv +0.007) (BLF test). Much cheaper alternative to the SBT90.2 with slightly lower performance. High Vf at high current makes FET/direct-drive and 1-cell buck drivers a poor match (Convoy).

emitters.name: XHP70.3 HI
emitters.notes_html: The go-to for high sustained output. ANSI bins 3000K–7000K plus EasyWhite 2700K–4000K (Cree datasheet). Domeless HI (3.9 mm source) roughly doubles intensity and cleans up the beam vs domed HD (5.3 mm source; 4,857 / 6,405 lm) (BLF Guide).

best_for.why_html: High efficiency at high drive means more lumens for the same heat. Sustained output is still set by the host's size and cooling

emitters.name: XHP50.3 HI
emitters.notes_html: ANSI bins 3000K–7000K plus EasyWhite 2700K–4000K (Cree datasheet). Compact quad-die workhorse; very efficient with decent throw, though tint can be a lottery (Convoy).

best_for.why_html: Best hotspot-to-spill balance; the multi-die alternatives give a wider spot and more lumens for less throw

emitters.notes_html: 5000K, 5700K or 6500K only (Cree). Cree's newer round-die (round LES) throw parts, with source sizes of 1.3–2.8 mm. Cree's direct answer to the SFT-25R / SFT-40 class. Few enthusiast tests yet.

emitters.name: XM-L2
emitters.notes_html: 2700K–7000K (Cree). The classic budget flooder, redesigned in 2021 as a flip chip ("the XM-L3 that never was"): much more efficient, lower Vf, and it survives ~17 A in overdrive tests. Same XM footprint, so existing boards and centering rings still fit. Luminance is only XP-L HD class and dedoming gains <10%, so it's a flood LED, not a thrower (koef3 test, BLF Guide).

best_for.why_html: High efficiency at high drive means more lumens for the same heat. Sustained output is still set by the host's size and cooling

emitters.name: XHP50.2 / XHP70.2
emitters.notes_html: ANSI bins 3000K–7000K, EasyWhite 2700K–5000K (Mouser). Older domed XHP generation: very bright but floody, with visible rainbow tint shift. Still sold by Convoy (Convoy Cree).

emitters.name: XFL series
emitters.notes_html: Cool and neutral only: ANSI bins at 5000K, 5700K and 6500K (Cree datasheet). Ultra-high-lumen domed multi-die parts for mega-flooders; mediocre colour.

best_for.why_html: 10,000–25,000 lm class with flood-only beams; NV1010 also offered in R9080 (availability varies)

emitters.name: W1
emitters.notes_html:
1 mm² die, cool white (~6000K). Unmatched pencil-beam throw for its size. The same package also comes in red, green, verdure, orange and blue (see §7) (BLF Guide, Convoy Osram).

Green (~520 nm green): Saturated true green; high perceived brightness, popular for hunting and signalling (Convoy Osram).

Verdure (lime/mint (phosphor-converted)): Spectrum centred near the eye's 555 nm sensitivity peak, so very high lumens per watt and a distinct "money green" tint (Convoy Osram).

Red (620 nm red): Red-orange; protects dark adaptation far better than white. For maximum night-vision preservation, deep red (660 nm, e.g. SST-20-DR) is better (Convoy Osram).

Blue (~445 nm blue): Short-wavelength blue throw emitter. Emisar/Noctigon also sell a W2 Deep Blue (Convoy Osram).

Orange (amber/orange): Warm monochrome option, used for wildlife watching and to cut glare in fog and rain (Convoy Osram).

emitters.name: SFN-43
emitters.notes_html: Extremely bright 5050 that competes with the XHP50.2; very high CCT (≈6000K) (BLF Guide).

emitters.name: SFN-55.2

emitters.name: SFH-43

emitters.name: FFL351A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.notes_html: Domeless flip-chip, ~2 × 2 mm chip, 4.3 mm² glowing area. Beam looks like a dedomed 519A with a slightly larger corona. Efficiency gains flatten above ~5 A. A newer run is reportedly less rosy than early batches. CCTs range from 1800K to 5000K (BLF test). In a 7-emitter light it beat a domed 519A by only ~3% in lumens, with negligible extra throw (1Lumen E07X).

emitters.name: FFL505A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.notes_html: Small round die (2.35 mm²) under glass, ringed by brittle white silicone. Same chip as the LMP W5050SQ3, so it's a Lumenpioneer part. Relatively high luminance for a warm high-CRI LED, but very inefficient: 31 lm/W at max, "probably the most inefficient modern 5050" the tester has measured. An SFT-40 3000K matches its throw at ~6 A. A 6500K / 97 CRI version also exists (BLF test, BLF 6500K test).

best_for.why_html: Rosy (FFL) or warm 95 CRI (SFT-40/70) alternatives to cool-white throwers; the YinDing is the rare cool-white high-CRI round die

emitters.name: FFL707A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.cri_html: "4000K" sample: 4277K, Ra 89, R9 49, Duv −0.016 (claimed −0.001). Another sample: Ra 97–98 (Opple meter)
emitters.notes_html: Four dies in the XHP70.3 HI footprint, but wired differently, so it needs its own board. Less flux and luminance than XHP70.3 HI. The gaps between dies can show a "donut hole" in smooth reflectors. ~9 A is the sensible limit. Samples vary a lot (BLF test).

best_for.why_html: High efficiency at high drive means more lumens for the same heat. Sustained output is still set by the host's size and cooling

emitters.name: FFL909A
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — Measured data
emitters.footprint_html: 9090 · listed as 3V (36 A max), but a near-identical part tests as ~9V
emitters.notes_html: 36 chips (the tested part was 3S × 12P). Listing claims 100 W, with 5000K Ra70 / 4000K Ra95 / 1800K Ra90 options. Very large emitting area (~71 mm²) means flood only, no throw. Possibly made by Hopthink. The FFL909MX variant (T9R, E90) is reported as brighter but greener (BLF test, BLF T9R).

best_for.why_html: 10,000–25,000 lm class with flood-only beams; NV1010 also offered in R9080 (availability varies)

emitters.name: FFL5009R
emitters.section: 6. Boutique & House-Brand Emitters (FireflyLite FFL, Noctigon NTG, LMP, Getian) — FireflyLite parts with seller data only
emitters.notes_html: Domeless quad-die "HI" part sold loose in 1800K / 2700K / 4000K / 5000K, plus a rosy 3500K in some lights. The listing gives Duv ±0.0005 for the original 4800–5300K bin. One reviewer reports Ra 95 / R9 97 for the 3500K L50 Sol, with no method stated. It's probably related to the Hopthink FL5009R that koef3 tested (3V, 11.8 mm² glowing area, 3,564 lm @ 20 A at 25 °C, Ra 94, R9 99, Duv −0.002, measured ~5900K). That test found a throwy all-rounder beam, but with a yellowish spot in smooth reflectors (FireflyLite, BLF FL5009R test, BLF L50 Sol review).
